title: TypeError: `_run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on websocket connect with `[USER].fragment(run_every=...)` in 1.58.0
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After Streamlit Cloud auto-installed **1.58.0** (released 2026-05-28), every websocket connect to a deployed app raises:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

The error is raised inside the threading wrapper installed by `add_script_run_ctx` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py`. The wrapper is defined as:

```python
def _run_with_thread_state() -> None:    # ← 0 positional args
    fields = getattr(thread, _FRAGMENT_THREAD_STATE_FIELDS_ATTR, None)
    if fields is not None:
        ThreadState.initialize(**fields)
    original_run()
thread.run = _run_with_thread_state
```

Something in the new threading path calls `_run_with_thread_state(arg)` with one positional argument, which the wrapper can't accept.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

[USER].fragment(run_every="5s")
def live_chart():
    st.write("tick")

live_chart()
```

Deploy to Streamlit Cloud (or run locally with Streamlit 1.58.0 on Python 3.13). The Sentry trace shows the error firing on every websocket connect even when no user-facing breakage is visible — the wrapped thread retries cleanly, so users don't crash, but Sentry floods.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit app with a `[USER].fragment(run_every="5s")` (or any positive interval) somewhere in the render path.
2. Open the app in a browser.
3. Observe `TypeError: _run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on every websocket connect.

### Expected Behavior

The fragment thread runs without raising; the auto-refresh works as it did in 1.57.0.

### Current Behavior

`TypeError` fires on every websocket connect. 51 events in 4 hours on our production deploy (5-user friends-alpha) before we pinned to 1.57.0.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Last known good: **1.57.0** (released 2026-04-28). Pinning to `streamlit==1.57.0` eliminates the error completely.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.13.13 (CPython)
- Operating System: Streamlit Cloud (Linux container) + reproduced on macOS 15.5
- Browser: Chrome 148 (also Firefox, Safari)

### Additional Information

Sentry trace excerpt:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
mechanism: threading
transaction: ws://[app].streamlit.app/_stcore/stream
```

Workaround: pin `streamlit==1.57.0` until a fix lands.

Happy to add more detail or test a candidate fix.

comments.body: Thanks for reporting this [USER], it looks like this error being triggered is specific to python 3.13 and also some other aspects of your environment -- I have not been able to reproduce it locally except in a unit test and our regression test for this path passes and is run in python 3.13. But, the fix is clear and I have made a PR. Once this is in a nightly maybe you can verify the fix?

## Analysis

This is a confirmed regression in Streamlit `1.58.0` affecting any app that uses `[USER].fragment(run_every=...)`. On every websocket connect, the threading wrapper installed by `add_script_run_ctx` raises `TypeError: _run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given`. As the reporter notes, the wrapped thread retries cleanly so end users don't see a visible crash, but Sentry/log pipelines get flooded.

**Likely root cause:** The wrapper was introduced in [PR #15072 (`[refactor][ParallelFragments] Introduce FragmentThreadState ContextVar`)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15072) and lives at `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py` (around L410-L418):

```412:418:lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py
def _run_with_thread_state() -> None:
    fields = getattr(thread, _FRAGMENT_THREAD_STATE_FIELDS_ATTR, None)
    if fields is not None:
        ThreadState.initialize(**fields)
    original_run()

thread.run = _run_with_thread_state  # type: ignore[method-assign]  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]
```

`Thread.run` can be invoked with arguments in some code paths (e.g. when a `Thread` subclass overrides `run`/`start` and forwards positional args, or `_bootstrap_inner` indirections during fragment scheduling), so the zero-arg signature is too strict. Changing the wrapper to `def _run_with_thread_state(*args, **kwargs)` and forwarding to `original_run(*args, **kwargs)` should fix this. Workaround in the meantime is to pin `streamlit==1.57.0` as the reporter did.

### Related Issues

- [#10805 Widget state is not persisted after adding `run_every` to a fragment](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10805) — Another `st.fragment(run_every=...)` runtime bug; same surface area but different symptom.
- [#10719 Nested periodic `st.fragment`s can cause `StreamlitDuplicateElementId`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10719) — Periodic-fragment scheduling/threading bug in the same code path.
- [#11971 SelectboxColumn in data editor not working when fragment with `run_every` is active](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11971) — Side-effect of the periodic fragment thread loop interfering with other features.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Independently confirming this on production traffic + verifying [PR #15376](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15376) resolves it.

**Production hit:** ~50 Sentry events in 4 hours on Streamlit Community Cloud after upgrading from 1.57.0 → 1.58.0. Same TypeError on websocket connect for a tab using `[USER].fragment(run_every="30s")`. Pinned back to 1.57.0 as a hot-fix.

**Bug repros cleanly on 1.58.0 with this distilled version of [the maintainer's regression test](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15376/commits/95a188951f):**

```python
import threading
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_run_context import (
    add_script_run_ctx, ThreadState,
)
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_requests import ScriptRequests
from streamlit.runtime.pages_manager import PagesManager
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_run_context import ScriptRunContext

pm = PagesManager("/main/script/path"); pm.set_pages({})
ctx = ScriptRunContext(
    session_id="test", _enqueue=lambda _m: None, query_string="",
    session_state=None, uploaded_file_mgr=None, main_script_path="/main/script/path",
    user_info={}, fragment_storage=None, pages_manager=pm,
    script_requests=ScriptRequests(),
)
ThreadState.initialize(fragment_id="test_fragment")

class T(threading.Thread):
    def run(self, *args): self.received = list(args)

t = T(); add_script_run_ctx(t, ctx)
t.run("test_arg")  # → TypeError on 1.58.0
```

Output on 1.58.0:
```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

**Verified the fix:** applied PR #15376's 2-line patch (`def _run_with_thread_state(*args, **kwargs)` + `original_run(*args, **kwargs)`) to the installed 1.58.0 — repro now passes cleanly, `t.received == ["test_arg"]`.

Holding off on the unpin until a release lands (currently still 1.58.0 on PyPI). Any sense of timing on a 1.58.1?
